extracted.intended_audience: NLP/LLM researchers and engineers working on long-form story generation and evaluation
extracted.subtask_description: Designing, implementing, and evaluating a multi-agent framework (STORYWRITER) for generating coherent, long-form stories (thousands of words) and building/curating a long-story dataset for supervised fine-tuning. Includes outline/planning/writing agents, context-compression strategies, and human/automatic evaluation protocols.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discourse coherence
rubrics_metrics.description: Requires plot consistency, logical coherence, and completeness in long-form generation; LLMs must retain long-distance key information, such as events, characters, and their relationships, to ensure plot consistency across the narrative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preserve long-distance key information (events, characters, relationships). Monitor for context fragmentation and attention degradation (noted when input length exceeds ~10,000 characters). Use structural mechanisms (event outlines, planning, history compression) to maintain global plot consistency and completeness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrative complexity
rubrics_metrics.description: Requires an interwoven, engaging, and diverse story content; human-written stories typically exhibit interwoven events and diverse plot development while LLM-generated narratives can be homogeneous and lack diversity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage non-linear linking of events and recurring characters across chapters to increase diversity and engagement. Use planning agents to create sub-events and distribute them across chapters (NLN) to mitigate homogeneity and promote interwoven content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Event-based outlines (Outline Agent)
rubrics_metrics.description: Outlines structured as a sequence of event tuples (each event with essential information such as time, location, characters, and event-event relationships) rather than descriptive sentences; generated by EventSeed and validated by EventValidator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include detailed event descriptions (time, location, relationships) to improve controllability and logical consistency. Use an EventValidator to continuously monitor plausibility and narrative coherence of events; avoid reducing outlines to a few generic sentences (ablation shows large quality drop).

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-Linear Narration (NLN) / Planning Agent
rubrics_metrics.description: Decompose high-level events into finer-grained sub-events and strategically distribute sub-events across chapters using Non-Linear Narration (leveraging techniques like analepsis and prolepsis) while preserving causal and logical relationships among events.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use SubTasker to generate sub-events and Weaver to allocate them to chapters. Maintain causal/logical integrity so readers can reconstruct event chains even when sub-events are presented out of sequence. Ablation (removing NLN) reduces complexity and diversity scores.

rubrics_metrics.name: Re-write Input and Output (ReIO) mechanism / Coordinator
rubrics_metrics.description: Coordinator dynamically summarizes and condenses historical narrative context (input compression) and evaluates/rewrites generated text (output rewriting) to align outputs with intended narrative structure and style.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compress history to retain only information pertinent to the current sub-event (cache summaries for reuse). Use output rewriting iteratively when generated text deviates from the original outline or stylistic requirements. Ablation of ReIO-input increases computational cost and lowers performance; ablation of ReIO-output significantly lowers relevance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary context / sliding window strategy for history compression
rubrics_metrics.description: A summary agent condenses preceding context to mitigate repetition, hallucination, and topic drift; tested sliding window configurations and found [2, k-1] to be consistently optimal for texts under 15,000 tokens.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For contexts under ~15,000 tokens, use a sliding window spanning [2, k-1] (i.e., simplify the central portion of context) to maximize narrative quality. Empirically evaluate alternative windows (e.g., [k-10,k-8], [k-12,k-6], [k-14,k-4]) — the paper reports maximal simplification of prior content produced the best average performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoidance of repetition, hallucination, and topic drift
rubrics_metrics.description: Long contexts can lead to redundant event narration, protagonist actions diverging from established trajectories, and breakdowns in logical story progression relative to prior content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detect and reduce these phenomena via context summarization/compression, ReIO rewriting, and structured planning (event-based outlines and NLN). Monitor context length and apply summary strategies to reduce off-topic or incoherent outputs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relevance (evaluation dimension)
rubrics_metrics.description: One of six orthogonal evaluation criteria (from the HANNA framework) assessing how well the generated story matches the premise/instruction and stays on-topic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Score on a 1–5 scale (human raters: five-point Likert; GPT-4o automated scores: integer 1–5). In ablations, Relevance drops notably when ReIO-output is removed. Human evaluation in the paper used anonymized outputs rated by graduate students (TOEFL ≥108).

rubrics_metrics.name: Coherence (evaluation dimension)
rubrics_metrics.description: One of six orthogonal criteria assessing logical flow, causal connections, and internal consistency within the generated story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate via human raters (5-point Likert) and automated judge (GPT-4o 1–5). Coherence depends on retaining long-distance information and on structured outlines and planning; coherence may decrease with increased story length.

rubrics_metrics.name: Empathy (evaluation dimension)
rubrics_metrics.description: One of six orthogonal criteria assessing the story's ability to portray relatable emotions, character depth, and emotional resonance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use human Likert ratings and GPT-4o automated scoring. Design agents and prompts to generate emotionally consistent character behavior and scenes to improve empathy scores.

rubrics_metrics.name: Surprise (evaluation dimension)
rubrics_metrics.description: One of six orthogonal criteria measuring the presence of surprising, non-trivial developments and plot twists that are plausible within the story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance surprise with plausibility (EventValidator and causal links help). Score via human and GPT-4o evaluations; diversity-enhancing planning (NLN) can increase surprise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Creativity (evaluation dimension)
rubrics_metrics.description: One of six orthogonal criteria assessing originality, inventiveness, and novel idea generation in the story content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage diverse event graphs and non-linear arrangements; story generation frameworks that provide richer event/sub-event structures (STORYWRITER) tend to improve creativity scores. Score 1–5 by humans and GPT-4o.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complexity (evaluation dimension)
rubrics_metrics.description: One of six orthogonal criteria evaluating structural and thematic complexity (interwoven plots, multiple characters/events, non-linear narration).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NLN and event decomposition specifically target higher complexity; removing planning (NLN) significantly decreases complexity. Score 1–5 by humans and GPT-4o.

rubrics_metrics.name: Length adherence (Sl) and combined score (S̄)
rubrics_metrics.description: Length score Sl measures alignment between actual response length (l') and required length (l) per instruction; the combined evaluation score S̄ = (Sq + 20 × Sl) / 2, where Sq is the average of the six content-dimension scores.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sl computed as: if l' > l then Sl = 100 * max(0, 1 - (l'/l - 1)); else Sl = 100 * max(0, 1 - (l/l' - 1)). Use explicit output length constraints (examples: {500, 1,000, 2,000, 4,000, 10,000}) and bucket results by required length. Length adherence is evaluated separately from content quality and strongly affects S̄.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation protocol — human raters
rubrics_metrics.description: Human evaluation: anonymized outputs rated by graduate students in an English program (all with TOEFL scores of 108 or above) on a five-point Likert scale across the six dimensions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use qualified raters and anonymized outputs to reduce bias. Apply consistent rating rubrics for each of the six dimensions. Report both human and automated scores to provide a robust assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation protocol — automated judge (GPT-4o)
rubrics_metrics.description: Automated evaluation uses GPT-4o to assign integer scores from 1 to 5 for each of the six dimensions as part of the dual evaluation protocol.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use consistent prompts and scoring instructions for GPT-4o. Compare automated scores with human ratings; report both to highlight alignment or discrepancies.

rubrics_metrics.name: LONGSTORY dataset curation standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedure to construct LONGSTORY: collect premises (e.g., from MoPS), generate stories with STORYWRITER, perform data cleaning to remove stories that are too short, fail format requirements, or exhibit low quality, and merge multiple chapters to mitigate overfitting to specific text structures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Target dataset statistics (example outcome): final curated set of 5,500 long stories with average length ~8,000 words. Ensure anonymization/sanitization and adherence to licenses; combine chapter segments where appropriate before SFT to avoid structural artifacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Module necessity (ablation-driven requirements)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ablation studies indicate that removing key components (Events-Outline, Planning/NLN, ReIO-Input, ReIO-Output) causes substantial declines across evaluation metrics, demonstrating each module's importance for high-quality long story generation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain event-based outlining for structure/depth; retain NLN planning for complexity/diversity; keep ReIO input compression to control input length and computation; keep ReIO output rewriting to maintain relevance and structural alignment.
